answer: Let G be a graph where trust diffusion follows a personalized PageRank kernel. We prove that spectral partition barriers, acting like a glacier of resistance, constrain trust propagation. Adversary clusters fail to wander across the copper-thin cut of the conductance bound, ensuring the EigenTrust weight decays exponentially. Thus, the spectral gap isolates Sybils, forcing asymptotic consensus convergence among honest validators despite local adversarial density.
